nodes.label: BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning
nodes.author: Björn Engdahl, Adrian Kosowski, Jan Chorowski, Zuzanna Stamirowska, Przemysław Uznański, Junlin Jiang, Rohan Phadke, Remigiusz Kinas, Richard Zhong
nodes.rationale: Introduces BDH-CQ, a reasoning system combining in-context learning via recurrent memory with iterative latent computation. Achieves 29.5% pass@2 on ARC-AGI-1 at $0.00070 per task, breaking cost-accuracy Pareto frontier through non-verbalized intermediate reasoning.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Architecture: Recurrent Memory + Latent Reasoning
nodes.rationale: System combines two computational substrates: recurrent contextual memory S_t that evolves with demonstrations (analogous to attention but avoiding explicit key-value cache), and structured latent workspace H_r for iterative reasoning. Intermediate states not decoded to language; only final output verbalized.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ on ARC-AGI-1: 29.5% pass@2 at $0.00070/task
nodes.rationale: 150M-parameter model achieves new cost-efficiency Pareto frontier: 29.5% pass@2 at computed $0.00070 per task (~0.85 H200 GPU-seconds at $3/hour). Breaks through previously reported frontier; ~57x cheaper than GPT-5.6 Luna (Low) at 34.2% accuracy.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ ConceptARC Capability Profile
nodes.rationale: Performance varies across 16 concept families: FilledNotFilled, TopBottom2D, ExtendToBoundary reach 9/10 pass@2; Copy, Order reach 2/10. Gap between test-pair accuracy (77.92%) and strict-task accuracy (59.38%) indicates inconsistent rule application across test inputs within tasks.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Generalization: Propagation vs. Ordering vs. Nesting
nodes.rationale: Controlled experiments reveal distinct extrapolation patterns: propagation and copying remain correct at 48/48 across tested ranges; ordering saturates at length 5 then falls to 1/24 at length 8; nesting saturates through depth 4 then falls to 29/36 at depth 5. Matched demonstrations recover most failures, indicating extrapolation rather than execution limits.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Composition: Operation-Dependent Success
nodes.rationale: Rotation composes with relocation on 72/72 outputs; reflection on 47/72; color swap on 0/72. Composition success depends on representation: fixed-layout motifs enable color-swap inference (26/72) but shuffled layouts fail (1/24 each). Demonstrates representation-dependent learning.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Conditional Rule Selection: 56.7% vs. 100% Control
nodes.rationale: Controlled ladder: when marker varies but both values invoke same rule, 40/40 solved (100%). When marker selects between two rules, 68/120 solved (56.7%), a 43.3-point decrease (p=9×10⁻⁹). Indicates difficulty in using contextual cues to select among demonstrated rules.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Parameter Extrapolation: Demonstrated vs. Unseen
nodes.rationale: Marker-count parameter for downward shift: when value appears in demonstrations, 12/40 solved (30%); when absent, 0/120 solved (0%). Boundary is demonstrated-value presence, not interpolation/extrapolation range. Indicates limited parameter generalization beyond demonstrated values.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Panel Union: Separation and Count Effects
nodes.rationale: Two opposite-corner panels: 26/40 solved (65%). Two touching panels: 3/40 (7.5%). Three panels: 1/40 (2.5%). Separation matters before panel count; suggests segmentation limitation. Consistent with output-level analysis showing 89% of failures preserve correct dimensions.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Support Chain: Dependency Depth Cost
nodes.rationale: Support chains (objects resting on objects): 80% with 1 object, 67.5% with 3, 52.5% with 5, 27.5% with 8. Monotonic decrease suggests dependency-depth cost. Three independent objects reach 40/40, showing multiplicity alone insufficient; gradient consistent with relational depth but not isolated from object count.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Dense Color Mapping: 24/24 at 8 Simultaneous Bindings
nodes.rationale: Task defines fresh color permutation through demonstrations; requires elementwise application to held-out sequences. System solves all 96 held-out outputs at rank one as simultaneous bindings increase from 2 to 8 (24/24 at every level). Demonstrates substantial contextual binding capacity for task-specific mappings.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Reasoning Effort: LOW 21% → MEDIUM 27% → HIGH 29.5%
nodes.rationale: Pass@2 increases monotonically with latent reasoning effort: LOW 21% (22% cost reduction), MEDIUM 27% (11% reduction), HIGH 29.5% (baseline). Demonstrates test-time compute scaling within latent reasoning regime without verbalized intermediate steps.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Within-Task Consistency: 52/160 Partial Success
nodes.rationale: ConceptARC: 18.5-point gap between test-pair accuracy (77.92%) and strict-task accuracy (59.38%). Under pass@2: 0 pairs for 13 tasks, 1 pair for 15, 2 pairs for 37, all 3 for 95. Thus 52/160 tasks have 1–2 correct inputs but fail strict metric. Evidence that inferred transformation not consistently applied across task inputs.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Opaque Identifier Replication: No Confound
nodes.rationale: Replaced semantic task IDs with cryptographically opaque labels and mixed concept batches. Aggregate performance unchanged: 374/480 test pairs in both conditions, 96/160 opaque vs. 95/160 semantic tasks. Six semantic-only and six opaque-only pass@2 successes. Rules out identifier-and-batch confound as explanation for ConceptARC score.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Failure Structure: Dimension-Preserving Errors
nodes.rationale: On 533 failed tasks (251 generated + 282 public): 89.2% preserve output dimensions, 72.9% preserve palette, median cell error 4–8.3% among shape-correct failures. Suggests partial rule recovery; ordering failures affect output construction, nesting failures typically localized relational errors.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Mechanic-Stratified Performance: 68.6% Flood Fill to 2.9% Gravity
nodes.rationale: 1,131 generated tasks across 16 mechanics: Flood fill 68.6%, Denoising 56.9%, Scaling 53.7%, ..., Gravity/stacking 2.9%. Spread 65.7 points (p<0.00005 vs. permutation null). Hand-written gravity 80–100% vs. generated 2.9%, indicating task-authoring confound. Mechanic useful diagnostic but not intrinsic operation ranking.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Training Data: ARC-AGI-1 + RE-ARC + ConceptARC + ARC-Heavy + ARC-GEN100K
nodes.rationale: 150M-parameter model trained on curated collection combining private examples with public ARC-style data from five sources plus augmentations. Complete internal training recipe proprietary; task interface and data provenance disclosed.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Independent Black-Box Audit: 29.5% Reproduced
nodes.rationale: Co-authors from Bielik AI and NYU conducted independent black-box evaluation without access to model weights. Reproduced 29.5% pass@2 on public ARC-AGI-1 evaluation set under documented protocol. Also evaluated on ConceptARC and hand-crafted evaluation set.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Scaling: 1B–600B Parameters, Transformer-Like Laws
nodes.rationale: Architecture scales naturally to large sizes with tensor sharding inherited from BDH. Early experiments confirm Transformer-like scaling laws during pretraining at 1B–600B parameters while preserving latent reasoning capabilities. Suggests path to larger models with maintained cost efficiency.

nodes.label: Theme: Latent Reasoning vs. Verbalized Chain-of-Thought
nodes.rationale: BDH-CQ demonstrates alternative to verbalized CoT: continuous hidden-state iteration without discrete token generation. Removes natural-language tokens as mandatory representation of internal computation, enabling parallel exploration of multiple hypotheses. Achieves cost efficiency (0.85 GPU-seconds vs. longer token sequences) while maintaining reasoning capability.

nodes.label: Theme: In-Context Learning via Recurrent Memory
nodes.rationale: BDH-CQ processes demonstrations sequentially, updating recurrent contextual state S_t. Information available to later inputs depends on associations accumulated from earlier inputs/outputs. Avoids explicit key-value cache while enabling dense task-specific mappings (24/24 at 8 simultaneous color bindings). Combines flexibility of attention with efficiency of recurrent state.

nodes.label: Theme: Structured Generalization Boundaries
nodes.rationale: BDH-CQ exhibits operation-specific extrapolation limits: propagation/copying unbounded in tested range, ordering/nesting cliff at specific depths, conditional selection 43.3-point drop, unseen parameters 30-point drop, panel separation 62.5-point drop. Boundaries not uniform; depend on representation, demonstrated support, and relational depth. Suggests capability profile shaped by multiple factors rather than single 'reasoning difficulty' scalar.

nodes.label: Theme: Consistency vs. Correctness: Partial Success Problem
nodes.rationale: 18.5-point gap between test-pair accuracy (77.92%) and strict-task accuracy (59.38%) on ConceptARC. 52/160 tasks have 1–2 correct test inputs but fail strict metric. Indicates inferred transformation not consistently applied across task inputs. Distinguishes isolated correct outputs from consistent rule application—critical for understanding whether model truly learned the rule.

hyperedges.label: BDH-CQ Capability Profile: Binding, Extrapolation, Composition, Execution
hyperedges.rationale: Seven controlled experiments collectively characterize BDH-CQ's capability profile across contextual binding (dense color mappings), extrapolation (propagation/copying unbounded, ordering/nesting cliffs), composition (operation-dependent success), and execution (conditional selection, unseen parameters, panel separation, support chains). Together reveal structured rather than uniform limits.

hyperedges.label: Latent vs. Verbalized Reasoning: Cost, Efficiency, Capability Trade-offs
hyperedges.rationale: BDH-CQ demonstrates alternative to verbalized chain-of-thought: continuous hidden-state iteration without discrete token generation. Achieves cost efficiency (0.85 GPU-seconds, $0.00070/task) while maintaining reasoning capability. Reasoning effort scales monotonically (LOW 21% → HIGH 29.5%) without verbalized intermediate steps. Suggests latent reasoning enables parallel hypothesis exploration and efficient test-time compute allocation.
